simple: A model is a container that groups parts and other objects into one thing, like a whole car, a house or a character. Grouping makes it easy to select, move and copy the whole object at once. This page shows how to make models, set a primary part, move models with scripts, and save them to Roblox to reuse or even sell. Almost every game object bigger than one part is a model.
analogy: A model is like a backpack. You can carry everything inside it with one hand, and you can still open it and take out one item when you need it.
keyPoints: Make a model by selecting objects and pressing Ctrl+G (Cmd+G), or by inserting an empty Model and dragging things into it. Ctrl+U (Cmd+U) ungroups it.
Characters are models: one Model holding the body parts, joints and scripts.
Set a PrimaryPart for models whose parts are joined, so the model's pivot and bounding box move with that part.
In scripts, move models with `PivotTo(cframe)`, `TranslateBy(offset)` or `MoveTo(position)`.
A model with a Humanoid and a part named Head shows a name and health bar above the head.
Parts that fall below `Workspace.FallenPartsDestroyHeight` are deleted, and the model is deleted too if its last part is gone.
With streaming on, models can be set to Persistent (never unloaded) or Atomic (loaded and unloaded all at once).
Right-click a model and choose Save to Roblox to upload it as an asset with its own ID that you can reuse or sell on the Creator Store.

terms.model: A container object that groups parts and other objects so they act as one thing in the Explorer.
terms.container: An object whose job is to hold other objects, like a folder.
terms.PrimaryPart: The part you choose as the model's main part. When the model moves, it moves based on this part.
terms.pivot: The point a model moves to and turns around. Without a PrimaryPart, it is the center of the model's bounding box.
terms.bounding box: The smallest invisible box that fits around everything in the model.
terms.CFrame: A value that stores both a position and a rotation. `CFrame.new(0, 10, 0)` means "at height 10, not turned".
terms.offset: How far to shift from where something is now. An offset of (0, 10, 0) moves a model from height 5 to height 15.
terms.selection cycling: Alt-click (Option-click) repeatedly to pick the parts hidden behind each other inside a model.
terms.FallenPartsDestroyHeight: A Y height. Parts that fall below it are deleted so they do not fall forever.
terms.streaming: Loading only the parts of the world near the player and unloading far-away parts to save memory.
terms.Persistent / Atomic: Streaming settings for a model. Persistent means it never unloads. Atomic means all of its pieces load and unload together.
terms.asset / asset ID: Something saved to Roblox's cloud, like a model, with a unique number you can use to insert it anywhere.
terms.dependency: Another asset a model needs, like a mesh, texture or sound inside it.
terms.restricted asset: An asset you can only use if you have permission. Without permission, it will not show or play in your game.

example.title: Move and turn a model with code
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (with a model named House in the Workspace)
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local house = Workspace:WaitForChild("House")

-- Lift the whole house up 10 studs, keeping its rotation
house:TranslateBy(Vector3.new(0, 10, 0))
print("Pivot is now at", house:GetPivot().Position)

task.wait(2)

-- Put the pivot at (50, 5, 0) and turn the house 90 degrees around the up axis
local target = CFrame.new(50, 5, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0)
house:PivotTo(target)
explain: `WaitForChild` waits until the House model exists, then gives it to us.
`TranslateBy(Vector3.new(0, 10, 0))` slides every part in the model up by 10 studs. If the pivot was at height 5, it is now at height 15. The rotation does not change.
`PivotTo` puts the model's pivot exactly at a CFrame. `CFrame.new(50, 5, 0)` is the spot, and `CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0)` adds a quarter turn around the up (Y) axis.
All parts keep their places relative to each other, so the house moves as one piece.

watchOut: Moving a model by changing each part's Position one at a time breaks it apart. Use `PivotTo` or `TranslateBy` to move the whole model.
Grouping parts into a model does not glue them. If parts are not anchored or welded, they still fall separately when the game runs.
If a model you used from someone else is invisible or silent in-game, it may use restricted assets your game has no permission for.
Models made with streaming in mind can suddenly vanish when a player walks away. Mark important ones Persistent.
